headline.label: 1.07× TypeScript execution time
headline.explanation: Geometric mean of 45 same-point warmed execution-time ratios across 23 source files. 1× is parity; lower is better. Direct JavaScript is the default in Phase53.

aggregation.note: Every one of the 45 benchmark points gets equal weight. A source may contribute multiple inputs; equal-source weighting gives 1.078×. The maintained corpus informed development and does not describe all Bend programs.

latest.timingFlagPolicy: Descriptive only: absolute half drift >20% or maximum/minimum fresh-round time >1.2. No rows excluded. Lack of flags is not proof of JIT convergence or statistical significance.

scopeNotes: Phase53 ordered02 is the installed compiler. Direct JavaScript is now the ordinary program/library output and --run route; --legacy-js retains mutable descriptors and G. Phase52 measured the direct backend while it was explicitly opt-in.

The45 fixed source/input benchmark cases remain unchanged. The direct backend uses the upstream-callable interface, without the additional legacy mutable descriptor ABI. Do not attribute the contract change to a semantics-preserving legacy optimization.
Phase46 was a six-source JS/C diagnostic, Phase49/50 were investigations, and they do not add a comparable new installed full45 runtime point.
Latest33 medians improve and12 regress against Phase52 direct06. All regressions are below3.4%;15 of45 points beat TypeScript,34 lie within±10%,39 within±20%. No row is excluded.

Six role/point timing flags remain. They describe fresh-round spread or half-window drift, not confidence intervals; an unflagged point does not prove JIT convergence. The maintained corpus is not an untouched holdout.
Near-parity average does not mean every program is at parity. The slowest point is a Mandelbrot grid case at1.911888× TypeScript; the fastest is Morning at0.868442×.
The latest paired speedup is1.055785×:5.58% more speed, equivalent to5.28% less execution time. Historical averages use their own same-run TypeScript references and are not pooled or multiplied.
historyNotes: No multiplication of incremental improvements; every value is computed directly against same-run pinned TypeScript.
P37/P39/P40 use historical/variation 1000ms warmup 300ms sample blocks and new application 600ms warmup 250ms blocks; later full-suite batches use1000ms warmup 300ms blocks.
P40 selects42 exact-byte reused comparisons and3 fresh checked06 raytrace comparisons.
P41 value is freshly measured as baseline in P42 report; its original phase report covers only6 inputs.
A descriptive snapshot trend, not a controlled causal comparison across campaigns. Every ratio uses a fresh same-run TypeScript denominator; no incremental gains are multiplied.

Phase52 introduces the upstream-compatible direct calling contract as an opt-in backend. Phase53 makes that backend the ordinary default. Legacy mutable-descriptor support remains a separately selected route.
Same benchmark IDs, source hashes and frozen catalog; generated modules and the complete-row observation adapter are backend-specific.
No new full45 checkpoint is inserted for campaigns46,49 or50, which did not publish a new comparable installed runtime score.

P51's historical average is higher than P48's, but its own fresh paired comparison improves3.007942× to2.927825× TypeScript. Use each release's paired control for causal interpretation; keep the observed historical trend unchanged.
